details.summary: An excellent, highly practical weeknight stew that cleverly uses Greek yogurt and red lentils to hit strict protein and saturated fat targets while delivering massive comfort in under 30 minutes. A minor tweak to the lentil volume would bring the excellent-quality carbohydrates strictly into the chapter's numerical ceiling.

dimensions.feedback: Flavors are well-balanced and make culinary sense. Classic Indian-inspired pairing of earthy lentils, tomatoes, and curry powder with a bright, tangy yogurt finish.
Every listed ingredient is used in the instructions exactly as described, and no unlisted ingredients appear.

Instructions are thorough. You provided clear time ranges, visual doneness cues ('deeply fragrant', 'wilt completely'), and crucially, included a short cooling rest to prevent the nonfat yogurt from splitting when added.
The recipe aligns perfectly with an Indian-inspired dal, using appropriate spices and aromatics.
Stovetop simmering in a single pot is the perfect method for quick-cooking red lentils.
Computed nutrition values are highly plausible and align well with the large portions of lentils and Greek yogurt.
The title matches the dish, and the intro is wonderfully practical, highlighting the time-saving prep and the smart swap of yogurt for coconut milk without making outsized health claims.
A very appealing, comforting weeknight dinner that relies on pantry staples and delivers creamy richness.
Brilliantly executes the diet's core philosophy: it provides high fiber and slow-digesting protein to stabilize blood sugar, while using unsaturated fat and nonfat dairy to protect the liver.

There is zero added sugar and the carbohydrate quality is exceptional. However, the 60.6 g total carbohydrate slightly exceeds the 55 g ceiling for the 'main' tier. To bring it strictly into the 32-55 g window without falling below the 26 g protein floor, consider reducing the dry red lentils from 4.2 oz (120 g) to 3.5 oz (100 g).
Perfectly hits the 'Vegetable & Meatless Dinners' brief. It creatively solves the vegetarian protein requirement (aiming for >26 g) by combining lentils with a generous portion of Greek yogurt.
Realistic timeline. Red lentils are genuinely a sub-20-minute ingredient, and leveraging pre-chopped onions ensures the prep stays well under the 30-minute total budget. No special equipment needed.
